Aerial

/AIR-ee-ul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Aerial means existing, happening, or moving in the air, or relating to aircraft.

Aerial means existing, happening, or moving in the air, or relating to aircraft. The drone's aerial footage revealed a pattern in the cornfield that no one had ever noticed from the ground.

Worked Example

Mapping the flood damage from the ground would have taken surveyors weeks of slogging through mud. Instead, the county hired a pilot to photograph the river valley from two thousand feet. In a single afternoon, the aerial survey captured every washed-out road and stranded farmhouse in crisp detail. Rescue crews used the photographs the next morning to plan their routes.

The survey was carried out from the air, by aircraft, which is exactly what aerial means.

How Aerial Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

airborne

airborne: carried or moving through the air

overhead

overhead: positioned above, in the air

Antonyms

terrestrial

terrestrial: existing on land

ground-based

ground-based: operating from the ground

How Strong Is It? — elevated → aerial → orbital

elevated vs. aerial

elevated vs. aerial: An elevated walkway rises above the street but stays fixed to the ground, while an aerial performer moves freely through the air itself.

orbital vs. aerial

orbital vs. aerial: An aerial photograph is taken from within the atmosphere, while an orbital one is captured from space, far beyond the air.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — aeri

Root — aeri: from Greek aer, air, borrowed into Latin as aer

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: characteristic of, pertaining to, having the nature of

Put it together

Put it together: Aerial joins the Greek root aer, meaning 'air,' with the suffix -al, meaning 'characteristic of.' Something aerial is literally 'characteristic of the air': existing in it, moving through it, or viewed from high within it.

Use the root in a new word: aerate

Use the root in a new word: aerate: Gardeners aerate compacted soil, literally working air into it, using the same Greek root aer.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, technical/descriptive register

Aerial commonly modifies views, photography, surveys, acrobatics, and attacks (an aerial view, aerial photography, an aerial stunt). In British English the word also serves as a noun for a radio or TV antenna, the rod that pulls signals out of the air.
